subject: Urgent Complaint - Wendell Apartments Creating Unsafe Conditions Near School
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council, Civil Enforcement Team, Mayor Mendenhall, SLCPD, and The Road Home, My name is Alexis Jesser, and I live near the Wendell Apartments at 204 W 200 N. I am writing to urgently raise concerns about the ongoing safety, public health, and criminal activity issues that occur daily at this facility and its surroundings. Despite its purpose as supportive housing, the Wendell Apartments have become a hotspot for: • Open drug use • Loitering and trespassing • Frequent and nearly daily police presence • Loud disturbances and aggressive behavior • Visible intoxication directly next to a school I have witnessed open drug use, loud fights, aggressive and threatening behavior, public intoxication near the school, and frequent police responses, sometimes multiple times a day. These ongoing problems are significantly impacting the safety and quality of life for residents and families in the area, especially given the school's proximity. I am requesting: 1. A formal investigation into the Wendell Apartments as a nuisance property 2. A review of the property's zoning compliance and safety standards, particularly considering its location next to a school 3. Immediate action by The Road Home to increase oversight, improve enforcement of rules, and hold tenants accountable for criminal or disruptive behavior 4. A public response outlining what steps city officials will take to restore neighborhood safety While I understand the importance of supportive housing, it cannot come at the expense of public safety and community well-being. If this facility cannot be managed in a way that protects the neighborhood, its operation should be re-evaluated. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I hope to see meaningful action taken soon. Sincerely, Alexis Jesser Resident near the Wendell Apartments

subject: SLC's Relationship with ICE
comment: Hello Councilman Wharton, My name is Jaycee, and I'm a Salt Laker in your district. I live in the aves near Java Jo's, a neighborhood that means a lot to both of us! I'm writing to you to encourage you in your role on the Salt Lake City Council to end Salt Lake City's contracts with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The council has a responsibility to ensure the city's relationships with federal agencies are ones that keep us all safe. The scale of the escalation of violent and extrajudicial abductions and deportations of civilians by ICE by this federal administration is unprecedented, and Salt Lake City has the opportunity to follow in the steps of other municipalities like Glendale, California and end all official contracts with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The city council in New York is considering investigating the NYPD's cooperation with ICE, and whether or not doing so has violated NYC's status as a sanctuary city. While Salt Lake City is not an official sanctuary city, a 2023 internal memo from Michael Bernacke, Salt Lake City ICE Field Office Director, revealed that ICE has ruled Utah to be a de facto Sanctuary State. Governor Cox has denied the allegations of the leaked memo, but Salt Lake City has the opportunity to impart meaningful protections by ceasing contracts with ICE and establishing a non-compliance policy for Salt Lake City PD when support is solicited by federal agencies to identify and detain individuals in immigration removal proceedings. Upon listening to your guest episode on City Cast Salt Lake this week, I understand your point about how the council and other leavers of municipal government walk a fine line between implementing progressive policies that Salt Lakers want at the risk of provoking retaliatory laws from our state legislature and the federal government. This is not the time to mind that fine line. There are families here who are Salt Lakers and Utahns through and through, just like you and me (I'm a sixth-generation Utahn, too), who are at risk of violent detention and deportation regardless of their immigration status, as we have seen reports of Americans with varied immigration statuses placed in removal proceedings. Every day that passes wherein Salt Lake City maintains these relationships with Immigration and Customs Enforcement jeopardizes our community safety. I wish you the best and hope to see you stand up for all Salt Lakers against the federal administration's action that puts many of us in harm's way. Best, Jaycee Miller

subject: Ongoing Noise Disturbance from Local Business – Request for Help
comment: Hi Council Member Dugan, I'm a resident near the Little Caesars on 2100 S, and I'm writing to ask for your help regarding a persistent noise issue that's been disrupting our neighborhood at night. Each evening, their rooftop furnace or HVAC system produces a loud, mechanical noise—deep, rumbling, and continuous. It often goes on well past midnight and severely impacts the sleep and quality of life for residents in the adjacent apartment building. So far, I have: Left two written notes at the store Submitted a formal complaint to Little Caesars corporate twice (no reply) Filed a noise complaint with Salt Lake City Code Enforcement and the County Health Department Notified police, who acknowledged the issue but said they could not intervene Despite all of this, the noise continues nightly without resolution. I'm reaching out to you in hopes that your office can help escalate this concern or connect me with the appropriate enforcement channel to ensure the business complies with nighttime noise ordinances. Thank you so much for your time—I truly appreciate your support. Best regards, Binh Nguyen
